demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- The offshore drilling market is in a two-speed recovery: high-specification deepwater/ultra-deepwater drillships are moving toward a tighter market while conventional and older semisubmersibles remain much more selective.
- The near-term offshore drilling market is softer than the 2023-25 peak, but the medium-term outlook is positive, particularly from 2027 onward.
- The fleet of drilling rigs is becoming more constrained, with limited newbuild activity gradually creating a supply-side constraint even without many new rigs being added.
- The market is increasingly separating into premium and non-premium assets, with Tier-1 drillships commanding higher day rates than older/lower-specification rigs.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The near-term offshore drilling market is described as softer than the 2023-25 peak, with recovery uneven across rig types (two-speed recovery) and some segments such as older jackups oversupplied in some regions.
- The Board has not recommended any dividend in view of accumulated losses from previous financial years and to conserve resources.
- The MD&A notes that Russia's offshore market, despite substantial resources, is affected by international sanctions, financing restrictions, insurance constraints, equipment limitations and geopolitical considerations, making it fundamentally different from conventional commercial offshore drilling.
- The UK offshore market is flagged as weaker than Norway due to declining production in mature fields, political uncertainty, energy-transition policy and higher regulatory pressure.
- The AGM notice proposes disinvestment of two wholly-owned overseas subsidiaries, Essar Shipping DMCC (Dubai) and OGD Services Holdings Limited (Mauritius), reducing the group's overseas subsidiary structure.
- Asia-Pacific offshore vessel markets are described as relatively volatile and have historically had lower utilisation than the Middle East and Northern Europe.
